title.narrative: Climate-smart pathways for an Agile and Resilient Economy [CARE]

description.narrative: Jordan, as the world's second-largest refugee host, grapples with economic challenges and resource strains. High unemployment and increasing poverty, affecting both Jordanians and Syrian refugees, pose significant socio-economic concerns, exacerbated by the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. Vision 2025 outlines ambitious development goals aiming for economic growth, reduced poverty, and unemployment rates. The National Green Growth Strategy, aligning with Vision 2025, focuses on transitioning to a green economy across six sectors. Its principles emphasize governance transparency, incentivizing green practices, integrated planning, and capacity building. Further, the Ministry of Environment's Strategic Plan prioritizes the transition to a green economy, aiming for sustainable growth, promotion of environmentally conscious practices, and the reduction of industrial wastewater through recycling for irrigation purposes. Jordan grapples with escalating water scarcity exacerbated by population growth, displacement, and climate change. If current trends persist, by 2025, per capita water supply might plummet from 145 m3/year to 91 m3/year, leading to a substantial deficit of 630 × 106 m3/year1, 12, 3. This scarcity threatens natural ecosystems, river basins, biodiversity, agriculture, water resources, human health, and socio-economic stability. Climate change impacts necessitate urgent action to safeguard Jordan's systems and people. The energy sector, crucial for economic growth, faces challenges due to limited fossil fuel resources and regional instability, putting pressure on water and transportation services. Nationally, Jordan aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 31% by 2030, with a 5% unconditional reduction. At the local level, cities grapple with unemployment, poverty, and resource constraints, stressing local authorities and exacerbating developmental and infrastructural challenges, particularly in water and energy sectors. The project "Climate-smart pathways for an Agile and Resilient Economy [CARE]" is centered on water, energy, food security, and ecosystem, using green finance, governance, and innovations. CARE takes a novel approach to address the above challenges by enabling the implementation of further green growth actions in Jordan under the bilateral envelope of the Jordan Multi-Annual Indicative Programme 2021-2027. The project will enhance synergies between the Green Growth Action Plan and other relevant sectoral plans, and will lead to a more efficient use of resources within a circular economy approach as well as reflect the water-energy-food Nexus themes. The project comes in alignment with EU Green Deal and the EU’s New Agenda for the Mediterranean, and its Economic and Investment Plan, focusing on the policy area for just green transition of climate resilience, energy and the environment. The proposed actions will be within the framework of the national plans and actions, such as the National Energy Efficiency Action Plans (NEEAPS), The Green Growth National Action Plan 2021-2025, and will contribute to the EU 2030 energy and climate targets across the 5 dimensions of the Energy Union: 1) Decarbonization, 2) Energy Efficiency, 3) Energy Security, 4) Research, Innovation and Competitiveness. The project will be implemented in Madaba which is located 35 km southwest of Jordan’s capital, Amman. It has an area of about 1,000 km2 and a population of approximately 200,000 in 2018. Madaba Governorate is divided into two directorates: Madaba directorate, which is 498.3 km2, and Deeban directorate, which is 543.6 km2. The direct beneficiaries include local farmers, and community in Madaba, as well as various stakeholders, municipalities. Additionally, the broader population in the target governorates will benefit indirectly from the Urban WEFE Nexus Lab. The project aligns with several Sustainable Development Goals, contributing to clean water and sanitation (SDG 6), affordable and clean energy (SDG 7), industry, innovation, and infrastructure (SDG 9), sustainable cities and communities (SDG 11), and climate action (SDG 13). By implementing innovative nature-based solutions and engaging local communities and educational institutions, the project seeks to create a lasting impact, promoting environmental stewardship and building resilient communities in the face of climate change challenges. In this project, UN-Habitat Jordan will be implementing an Urban-WEFE Nexus Lab referred to as Nex-L. The intervention aims at the production and co-demonstration (actions carried out with stakeholders) of water-energy-food-ecosystem Nexus asset plans for a just and sustainable allocation of natural resources, where practical experimentation sites will be created, called Urban-WEFE Nexus Lab (Nex-L). Ideally, Nex-L will be established on a 7 Dunum public space (7000 sq.m) to the east of Madaba beside the eastern police center on a land granted by the municipality as an In-kind donation.
